Night of day 1: player_1 was stabbed by the serial killer last night. They were a chanteuse.

It's a massive break for us that the Serial Killer took out a wolf on night one. Since player_1 was the Chanteuse, their block went through before they died. If anyone was blocked or has investigative info, now is the time to start sharing so we can build some leads.

Night of day 2: player_8 was attacked by the wolves and the serial killer but was saved by the healer! The Speculator has picked Town.

I am the Sentinel, and I watched player_8 last night. They were visited by player_3, player_4, player_7, and player_10, meaning our Healer, the Wolf carrier, and the Serial Killer are all in this group.

player_2 is telling the truth. I am the Trailseer, and I followed player_8 last night, which explains my visit. Since player_8 was attacked by both the wolves and the Serial Killer and saved by the Healer, the other three visitors player_2 saw—player_4, player_7, and player_10—must be the Healer, the Serial Killer, and the last remaining wolf (the Illusionist). We have our targets.

I am actually the Healer, and I protected player_8 last night. That explains my visit perfectly. Since player_3 is the Trailseer, this means player_7 and player_10 must be the Wolf carrier and the Serial Killer.

Player_4 is lying. I am the real Healer, and I protected player_8 last night. Since player_4 is fake-claiming my role to cover their visit, player_4 is definitely one of the attackers (either the Wolf or the SK), and player_10 is the other. We should eliminate player_4 today.

Player_7, you're counter-claiming because you got caught red-handed by player_2's watch and had to scramble for a defense. If you were actually the Healer, you wouldn't have waited for me to claim first before throwing out your accusation. You and player_10 are the two attackers from last night.

Player_4, claiming first doesn't make you the healer; it just means you scrambled to claim the role first to cover your tracks once player_2's watch was revealed. We speak in the order the moderator chooses, so of course I had to wait my turn to speak. I am the actual Healer who saved player_8, which makes you and player_10 the attackers.

Player_7, you only claimed after seeing the heat was on you and player_10. Real healers don't wait to see which way the wind blows before explaining their visit. Notice how player_10 is staying completely silent while you try to shift the blame?

I am the Sigilist, and I placed a sigil on player_8 last night to catch anyone targeting him, which explains my visit. Since I am the Sigilist and player_8 was attacked twice, the math doesn't add up if we assume player_2, player_3, and player_4/7 are all telling the truth. One of those 'confirmed' claims is a wolf trying to slide by.

player_10, that is not how the Sigilist works. A sigil strikes the player it is placed on if *that* player attacks someone, not the people targeting them. Since you completely misunderstood the role you are claiming, you are clearly lying to cover your visit.

You're right about the mechanics, player_3, but you misunderstood my intent because I misspoke. I placed the sigil on player_8 because I suspected he might be an attacker, hoping to catch him if he went out to strike. My slip of the tongue doesn't change the fact that player_4 and player_7 are in a direct 1v1 over the Healer claim, which is where our focus should be.

player_10, your cover story doesn't work because I am the real Sigilist, and I haven't placed any sigils yet. You scrambled to claim my role because you got caught visiting player_8 and couldn't claim Healer. We should eliminate player_10 today; they are 100% one of the attackers.

player_5, you are jumping on an easy opportunity to construct a fake counter-claim and divert attention from the Healer conflict. If player_4 and player_7 are in a direct 1v1, one of them is 100% evil. By trying to execute me instead, you're protecting whichever wolf is caught in that Healer pair.

player_10, calling my counter-claim a 'diversion' is a weak attempt to save yourself. You got caught visiting the attack target, botched the mechanics of the role you tried to steal, and now you're upset that the real Sigilist is standing up. Eliminating a 100% confirmed fake-claimer like you is always the correct move over guessing a 50/50 Healer split.

player_5, your counter-claim is incredibly convenient. With player_4 and player_7 in a hard 1v1, one of them is 100% a wolf. By trying to push the town to execute me instead, you are actively protecting your partner in that Healer pair. If we want a guaranteed evil elimination today, we must resolve the Healer 1v1.

player_10, your theory makes no sense. If I were a wolf trying to protect a partner in the healer 1v1, counter-claiming you and putting myself in the spotlight is the worst possible way to do it. You tried to steal my role, got the mechanics completely wrong, and now you are desperate. Eliminating you is a guaranteed evil, while guessing between player_4 and player_7 is a coin flip.

player_10, your excuse for placing a sigil on player_8 makes no sense. Why would you suspect player_8 of being an attacker on Night 2 when nothing happened on Day 2 to make them suspicious? You got caught visiting the victim, messed up the mechanics, and player_5's counter-claim seals it. We should eliminate player_10 today.

player_6, player_8 was the obvious choice to sigil because after player_1's death on Night 1, they were the most logical target for any overnight actions. More importantly, player_5's instant counter-claim is too convenient. By focusing on me, player_5 is actively trying to shut down the healer 1v1, which guarantees we execute a wolf today if we resolve player_4 versus player_7.

As the person who was actually attacked last night, I can confirm player_2's watch is spot on. I had exactly four visitors: the Trailseer, the true Healer, and my two attackers (the Wolf and the SK). This leaves absolutely no room for player_10's Sigilist claim to be true, especially with player_5 counter-claiming. Player_10 is guaranteed evil and we should eliminate them today.

player_8, think about the math. If player_3 is the Trailseer and I am the Sigilist, then player_4 and player_7 are the Healer and the Wolf attacker. This means one of them is 100% a wolf. If you execute me, you let a confirmed wolf in that Healer pair walk free for another night to kill again.

I am the Investigator. I checked player_7 last night and they read Not suspicious. This means player_7 is mathematically cleared of being the Wolf carrier. Between player_4 and player_10, at least one of them must be the wolf. Since player_10's Sigilist claim makes no sense with the visitor count, we should eliminate player_10 today.

player_9, your check on player_7 actually solves this game. If player_7 is Not suspicious, they are the true Healer, which means player_4 is guaranteed to be the Wolf carrier who attacked player_8. We have a 100% confirmed Wolf in player_4 right now; we should eliminate them immediately instead of chasing unproven claims.

Player_10's push to resolve the Healer 1v1 today is just a distraction to save themselves. We know for a fact that player_8 only had four visitors: the Trailseer, the true Healer, and the two attackers. There is mathematically zero room for a Sigilist, making player_10 guaranteed evil regardless of who the real Healer is. We should take the 100% guaranteed evil elimination on player_10 today.

player_2, you are ignoring the mathematical certainty player_9 just handed us. If player_7 is verified 'Not suspicious' by the Investigator, they cannot be the wolf carrier, which means player_4 is 100% the wolf carrier who attacked player_8. Even if you doubt my Sigilist claim, executing player_4 guarantees we put a wolf in the ground today, while letting them live guarantees another wolf attack tonight.

Player_10, your logic completely falls apart because you forgot how the Serial Killer works. The SK also reads 'Not suspicious' to the Investigator. That means player_7's result doesn't make them the confirmed Healer at all; they could easily be the SK who attacked player_8 and is now fake-claiming Healer to escape. You are still the caught liar here, and we should eliminate you today.

Player_4, your SK theory is a desperate attempt to explain away player_9's check on me. If I were the SK who attacked player_8, I wouldn't have known player_8 was going to be saved, making a Healer fake-claim incredibly risky. I am the actual Healer. That said, player_10 is a completely caught liar after botching the Sigilist mechanics and getting counter-claimed by player_5. We should eliminate player_10 today for a guaranteed evil, and resolve our 1v1 tomorrow.

Player_7, I claimed first because I had nothing to hide, and I know I protected player_8. But regardless of our 1v1, player_10 is a mathematically proven liar who botched the mechanics of the role they tried to steal. We should absolutely execute player_10 today and not let them distract us.

player_4, your theory that player_7 is the Serial Killer is an absurd stretch to save your own skin. An actual Serial Killer has absolutely no reason to counter-claim Healer and force a deadly 1v1 when they could just lay low. You are mathematically the Wolf carrier who attacked player_8, and trying to deflect onto player_7 or me won't change that.

You're still ignoring the glaring hole in your logic, player_10. If player_7 is the SK, their Not suspicious result is completely expected, and they easily could have fake-claimed Healer once player_2 posted the visits. But more importantly, you got caught lying about being Sigilist by the actual Sigilist, player_5. Trying to force a 50/50 on the Healer claim won't save you from being a mathematically proven fake.
Before the vote: player_10 has been accused by player_3, player_4, player_5, player_6, player_8, player_9, player_2 and player_7; player_4 by player_3, player_7 and player_10. Each gets a last word.

Town, please look at the mathematical certainty we have right now. Player_9 verified player_7 is Not Suspicious, which confirms player_7 is our real Healer, leaving player_4 as the absolute guaranteed Wolf carrier who attacked player_8. If you eliminate me, you are letting a 100% confirmed Wolf walk free to kill again tonight, whereas executing player_4 guarantees a Wolf down.

Eliminating player_10 is our only 100% guaranteed evil vote today because their Sigilist claim is mathematically impossible and directly counter-claimed by player_5. Player_7's 'Not suspicious' result does not clear them of being the Serial Killer, who also registers as clean to the Investigator. I protected player_8 as the Healer, and we must secure the guaranteed catch on player_10 before resolving anything else.

Here's the vote result for day 3:
  player_2 voted to eliminate player_10
  player_3 voted to eliminate player_10
  player_4 voted to eliminate player_10
  player_5 voted to eliminate player_10
  player_6 voted to eliminate player_10
  player_7 voted to eliminate player_10
  player_8 voted to eliminate player_10
  player_9 voted to eliminate player_10
  player_10 voted to eliminate player_4
Player player_10 has been voted out and was a serial killer.
Night of day 3: player_4 was attacked by the vigilante and a sigil last night. They were a illusionist. player_7 was killed by the wolves last night. Their role is hidden by an illusionist.
Game over! The town has won! The speculator won.
